United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Strengthening the scientific capacities of young Yemeni researchers by providing remote access to scientific knowledge, research infrastructure, laboratory facilities, data, and international scientific collaboration opportunities through Open Science and remote laboratory access mechanisms.

description.narrative:
Yemen's prolonged crisis has severely affected its higher education and scientific research systems, limiting the ability of universities and research institutions to generate knowledge, support innovation, and contribute to national recovery efforts. Young researchers face significant barriers, including limited access to scientific literature, research data, laboratory facilities, advanced analytical equipment, funding opportunities, and international scientific networks. These challenges have contributed to the isolation of the country's scientific community and constrained the development of evidence-based solutions to pressing national challenges such as water scarcity, food insecurity, climate change, environmental degradation, renewable energy, and disaster risk reduction.
The UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science and the UNESCO Remote Access to Lab Equipment initiative (UNESRALE), offer a practical mechanism for addressing one of the most critical gaps facing Yemeni researchers: access to modern scientific infrastructure. Through remote access technologies, researchers can utilize sophisticated laboratory equipment hosted by partner institutions worldwide without the need for costly travel or physical presence. This approach enables Yemeni scientists to conduct experiments, acquire technical skills, engage in international research collaborations, and contribute to high-quality scientific outputs despite the challenging national context.
Key Activities:  Improvement of access to Open Scientific Knowledge and Research Resources for Yemeni scientists.  Remote access to international laboratory facilities through UNESRALE.
Key beneficiaries:  Researchers, scientists, and academics from universities, research centers, and technical institutions.  Young professionals and students, particularly those pursuing STEM-related fields. Key partners:  Yemen National Commission.  UNESCO Headquarters and Field Offices.  Yemeni Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research.  Yemeni universities and research centers.  UNESRALE partner laboratories and universities.  International research organizations and scientific networks.  Arab and Gulf universities and research institutions.
